findings.issue: Wrong reading of 何: before を it is read なに, not なん (なん appears only before t/d/n sounds or counters, e.g. 何ですか, 何人). The kana transcribes 何を as なんを.
findings.current: なんをすることになっているかわからない。
findings.suggested: なにをすることになっているかわからない。

findings.issue: Token 何 is glossed as the object of する followed by を; in this position 何 is read なに, not なん.
Romaji propagates the wrong reading of 何 ('nano' = nan+o); should reflect なにを (nani o).
Accent error: 'quê' takes the circumflex only at the end of a phrase/before a pause or as a noun; mid-clause it must be 'o que está'.
findings.current: Não entendo o quê está combinado que se faça.
findings.suggested: Não entendo o que está combinado que se faça.

findings.issue: Sense-changing misreading: 欲しがっている means 'is showing signs of wanting (a car)'; 'keeps showing off his own car' claims he flaunts a car he already owns, misreading がる as 'show off'. Contradicts en/pt and the (correct) explanations.
findings.current: My friend [topic] keeps showing off his own car [object] (showing-off-te wanting state).
findings.suggested: My friend [topic] a car of his own [object] is showing signs of wanting (がる + ている state).

findings.issue: しか…ない means 'only / nothing but a few exist'; 'there aren't even a few' renders 少しも…ない (not even a few), the opposite quantity implication, and contradicts the parenthetical it carries.
findings.current: As for friends, there aren't even a few (= I have only a few).
findings.suggested: As for friends, apart from a few, there are none (= I have only a few).

findings.issue: 'many friends' is unsupported: 友人たち is only plural 'friends'; たくさん quantifies 時間 (already rendered as 'plenty'). A learner may wrongly attach たくさん to the friends; expl correctly attaches it to time.
findings.current: I had plenty of time to talk to many friends.
findings.suggested: I had plenty of time to talk with my friends.

findings.issue: Spurious structure: 'It's to the point that' implies a degree construction (ほど/まで) absent from the JP; いなくなる is simply 'will come to not exist'. Also switches person ('I'll have no friends') while en/pt read 'you'.
findings.current: It's to the point that I'll have no friends, you know.
findings.suggested: Friends [subject] will come to not exist, you know.

findings.issue: Literal mirror drops the first verb いて (te-form of いる 'stay') entirely and invents 'falls'; lit_pt correctly keeps it as 'ficando'. The stay-then-watch structure is the point of the sentence.
findings.current: Until night falls, let's go see the fireworks!
findings.suggested: Staying until night, let's go watch the fireworks!

findings.issue: Garbled gloss for い (stem of いる 'to be/stay'): いる never means 'become (lively)'. Looks like a mistranslation of the pt gloss 'ficar presente (ser animado)' where 'ser animado' = 'animate being'.
Pronoun clashes with en/pt ('She played…', 'Ela tocou…'); the JP subject is implicit, so all translation fields of the record should use the same person.
findings.current: As promised, he played the piano.
findings.suggested: As promised, she played the piano.

findings.current: O sujeito (ela) fica implicito, algo comum em japonês.
findings.suggested: O sujeito (ela) fica implícito, algo comum em japonês.

findings.issue: Missing accent: 'nucleo' should be 'núcleo' (spelled correctly elsewhere in the batch).
